question: How do you approach optimizing slow code?

scenes.sub: Measure first. Fix the biggest cost. Measure again.
scenes.say: Performance optimization. The wrong answer is guessing. The right answer starts with a measurement.

scenes.head: Think of a slow commute
scenes.say: Your commute is slow. You time each part. Walking, five minutes. Traffic, fifty minutes. Parking, two. Buying a faster car won't help. You fix the biggest part. Code is the same: a profiler is the stopwatch that shows which part eats the time.

scenes.head: A profile of a slow script

panels.code:
def main():
    data = load()          # read and parse
    if has_dup(data):      # suspect
        print("duplicates")

output.text:
has_dup    4.2 s
load       0.1 s
print      0.0 s

scenes.say: Run the profiler, for example c Profile, sorted by time. These numbers are an illustration. The report says has dup takes four seconds, load a tenth, print nothing. So has dup is the only place worth touching.

scenes.head: Algorithm beats constant factors

panels.code:
# before: O(n^2)
def has_dup(xs):
    for i, x in enumerate(xs):
        if x in xs[:i]:      # copy + scan
            return True
    return False

# after: O(n) on average
def has_dup(xs):
    seen = set()
    for x in xs:
        if x in seen:        # O(1) average
            return True
        seen.add(x)
    return False

scenes.say: The cause: for each element it copies a slice and scans it. That is O of n squared. With a hundred thousand items, that is about five billion steps. A set of seen values makes each check O of one on average, so about a hundred thousand steps. Same answer, thousands of times faster.

scenes.head: In the interview: follow-ups
rows: Measure with a profiler on realistic input.
Algorithm first. Tweaks give maybe two times.
I O: fewer database calls, caching, batching.
Optimizing by guess, or a part that is two percent of runtime.
scenes.say: Likely follow-ups. Where do you start? Measure with a profiler on realistic input. Loop tweaks or algorithm? Algorithm first. After that? I O: fewer database calls, caching, batching. The common mistake: optimizing by guess, or tuning a part that is two percent of the runtime.

lines: I measure first and never guess the bottleneck.
I fix the biggest cost; algorithms beat constant factors.
Then I measure again and keep the code readable.
scenes.say: I measure first and never guess the bottleneck. I fix the biggest cost, since algorithms beat constant factors. Then I measure again and keep the code readable.
